features.name: Configurable embedding provider + offline/no-network fallback
features.behavior: get_embedder() (src/braintodo/api/nodes.py) reads settings.embedding_provider ('sentence_transformer' default | 'fake'). SentenceTransformerProvider wraps model-load OSError in a clear, actionable RuntimeError instead of a raw huggingface.co connection stack trace. Fixes a real gap: production always hardcoded the real SentenceTransformerProvider with no fallback, but every existing test overrode get_embedder with FakeEmbeddingProvider, so this path had never been exercised by any test in any session - a network-restricted deploy would 500 on every POST /nodes despite a fully green suite.
features.evidence: Discovered 2026-08-24: after installing torch/torch-geometric/sentence-transformers for the first time in any session and running the FULL suite (not the fast/excluded suite), confirmed get_sentence_transformer_provider() raises a raw OSError connecting to huggingface.co in this network-restricted sandbox - i.e. F001 (Node CRUD) would 500 on every create in an offline deploy despite being marked passing. Fixed via EMBEDDING_PROVIDER setting + FakeEmbeddingProvider fallback + clear RuntimeError. Verified both directions: (1) default 'sentence_transformer' with no network reachable raises RuntimeError with actionable message (was raw OSError before fix); (2) EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=fake exercised through the REAL api.nodes.get_embedder -> NodeRepository dependency-injection path (not a test override) successfully returns 201 on POST /nodes with a real embedding vector. Full suite re-run after fix: 118 passed, 1 skipped (test_neo4j_store.py self-skips, no live Neo4j in this sandbox), ruff check . clean. UPDATE 2026-08-25: a second session (running on a machine with real internet access, unlike this sandbox) caught a real gap in the original test_sentence_transformer_unreachable_raises_actionable_error test - it asserted real network failure rather than mocking it, so it only passed in a network-restricted environment and would have tried to genuinely download the model (slow/flaky, and not actually testing the error-wrapping logic) on any machine with working internet. Fixed by monkeypatching sentence_transformers.SentenceTransformer to raise OSError, making the test hermetic regardless of the running environment's actual network state. The same session also resolved the previously-flagged pre-existing mypy error (SentenceTransformerProvider.dimension: int | None vs int) via an explicit dimension: int class annotation + int(dim) if dim is not None else 384 fallback. Both fixes independently re-verified in a torch-installed sandbox (not just trusted from the reporting session, which had only run the fast/--ignore suite and not the full one): pytest -q -> 118 passed, 1 skipped (unchanged); ruff check . -> clean; mypy src tests -> 0 errors in 85 files (previously 1 pre-existing error, now genuinely resolved, not just claimed).

features.name: Clustering service upgrade: Leiden algorithm + configurable resolution + semantic cluster labels
features.behavior: ClusterService rewritten to use the Leiden algorithm (via python-igraph + leidenalg) instead of Louvain (networkx.algorithms.community.louvain_communities) - Leiden guarantees internally well-connected communities and converges faster; Louvain can produce internally-disconnected communities, a known algorithmic weakness. detect_clusters(owner_id, resolution=1.0) now accepts a resolution parameter (higher -> more, smaller clusters; lower -> fewer, larger ones), exposed on GET /clusters as an optional ?resolution= query param (validated > 0, 422 otherwise). The Cluster model gains a `label: str | None` field: a human-readable name derived from the cluster's member node embeddings (the node closest to the cluster's embedding centroid by cosine similarity becomes the label, e.g. 'Auth flow' instead of 'Cluster 3'), reusing each node's already-computed F003 text embedding rather than re-embedding anything. label is None when no member node has an embedding yet, so callers fall back to a numeric label themselves rather than being handed a fabricated one. Frontend GraphCanvas.jsx wired to prefer this label over the old hardcoded numeric 'Cụm N' text when present.
features.evidence: 2026-08-25. Implemented per the universe-theme roadmap (F022 was the one genuine backend feature in that plan - see Decisions.md). Installed python-igraph and leidenalg, verified smoke-test behavior directly before building on them (two-triangle split, isolated-node singleton, empty-graph, determinism-with-fixed-seed - all matched the prior Louvain implementation's expected outputs exactly). All 4 pre-existing test_clustering.py tests and both pre-existing test_clusters_api.py tests pass UNMODIFIED against the new algorithm. Added 9 new backend tests: resolution parameter accepted + deterministic, higher resolution produces >= as many clusters (bridge-graph case), label uses the title of the node closest to the embedding centroid (verified against a 'far outlier' embedding to confirm it's not just picking an arbitrary member), label is None with no embedded members, label falls back correctly for a single embedded member, plus 4 direct unit tests for the _cosine_similarity/_centroid helper functions (identical vectors, orthogonal vectors, zero-vector no-crash, centroid averaging). Added 2 new API tests: resolution query param accepted, resolution <= 0 rejected with 422. Fixed one real mypy gap surfaced by the new code (Node.embedding is list[float] | None; the list-comprehension filter didn't narrow the type for mypy) by carrying the narrowed embedding alongside its node in tuples rather than re-accessing the possibly-None field. Frontend: wired GraphCanvas.jsx to use cluster.label when present, added a regression test proving the semantic label takes priority over the numeric fallback and that a null label still falls back correctly (not rendering the literal string 'null'). Full verification: pytest -q (backend) -> 129 passed, 1 skipped (up from 118); ruff check . -> clean (caught and fixed an import-ordering issue and an unused test variable before landing clean); mypy src tests -> 0 errors, 85 files. npm run test (frontend) -> 19 files, 117 passed (up from 116); npm run build -> 619 modules, clean; npm run lint -> 0 warnings/0 errors, 49 files.

features.name: Optional: persisted 3D node layout position (x, y, z)
features.behavior: Node model gains optional x, y, z float fields so a 3D layout position can be persisted and stay stable across reloads/sessions, instead of being recomputed from scratch by the client's force simulation every time. Deliberately optional/low-priority: the 3D graph view (FE025) works today with a purely client-computed, ephemeral layout (matching how the existing 2D d3-force layout already works) - this feature only matters if users want their 3D arrangement to persist rather than re-settle on every load.
features.evidence: Planned 2026-08-25. Deliberately deferred/optional: confirmed the 3D graph requirement (FE025) does NOT require any backend change to function - 3D layout, like the existing 2D layout, can be computed entirely client-side from the same /nodes and /edges data already served. This entry exists only to track the persistence enhancement if it's later wanted, not as a blocker for FE025.

features.name: Task fields on Node
features.behavior: Node model gains node_type ('idea' | 'task', default 'idea'), due_date, priority, completed_at, and recurrence_rule fields. No new table or Postgres migration needed - Node data lives entirely in the GraphStore (Neo4j/in-memory), and both store implementations serialize Node via generic model_dump(), so adding fields to the Pydantic model was sufficient. Existing idea-nodes are unaffected (node_type defaults to 'idea', task fields stay null). completed_at is settable via NodeUpdate/Node but intentionally NOT exposed on NodeCreate - creating an already-completed task is out of scope, deferred to F025's complete endpoint.
features.evidence: Verified on a fresh clone of main. Confirmed via code reading (not assumed) that Postgres/db/models.py holds only User/EmailVerificationToken - Node has no Postgres table, so no Alembic migration was needed; both InMemoryGraphStore and Neo4jGraphStore persist Node via node.model_dump(), so the new fields round-trip through both backends with zero store-layer changes. Added 6 tests to tests/test_nodes.py: default node_type, task-field round-trip, invalid priority/recurrence_rule/node_type -> 422, and idea-node update leaving task fields untouched. Fast suite: 105 -> 111 passed. Full suite (incl. torch/Neo4j-dependent tests): 129 -> 135 passed, 1 skipped (test_neo4j_store.py self-skips, no live Neo4j in this session - not exercised end-to-end against real Neo4j). ruff check . -> clean. mypy src tests -> 0 errors, 85 files.

features.name: Task completion endpoints + task-filtered listing
features.behavior: PATCH /nodes/{id}/complete sets completed_at (via a dedicated GraphStore.complete_node, not the general update path); PATCH /nodes/{id}/reopen clears it via GraphStore.reopen_node. GET /nodes accepts an optional ?type=idea|task filter, owner-scoped, reusing F014's pagination. Both endpoints are generic to any Node (not type-restricted to 'task') and 404 identically for another user's node, per F020's ownership-is-not-leaked convention.
features.evidence: Verified on the same fresh clone as F024. Discovered mid-implementation that a plain PATCH through NodeUpdate cannot clear completed_at back to null - both store update_node() implementations use model_dump(exclude_unset=True, exclude_none=True), so an explicit None is silently dropped, not applied. Added dedicated GraphStore.complete_node()/reopen_node() protocol methods instead of routing reopen through NodeUpdate; Neo4jGraphStore.reopen_node uses Cypher REMOVE (Neo4j has no null-valued properties, only present/absent). Added node_type filtering to list_nodes_paginated in both InMemoryGraphStore and Neo4jGraphStore. Added 8 tests to tests/test_nodes.py: complete sets completed_at, reopen clears it, 404 on nonexistent node for both, 404 (not 403) when completing another user's node, and ?type= filtering (task-only, idea-only, unfiltered counts). Fast suite: 111 -> 117 passed. Full suite: 135 -> 141 passed, 1 skipped. ruff check . -> clean (one unused-noqa caught and removed mid-session). mypy src tests -> 0 errors, 85 files (one real invariance error caught mid-session: passing **dict[str, object] to neo4j's AsyncSession.run() needs a Mapping, not dict, due to variance - fixed by passing plain kwargs instead of unpacking a shared params dict).

features.name: Daily task query
features.behavior: GET /tasks/today returns the caller's task-nodes (node_type=='task') that are due today or overdue (due_date <= today) and not completed (completed_at is None), owner-scoped. New /tasks router, registered in main.py alongside the existing routers.
features.evidence: Verified on the same fresh clone as F024/F025. New src/braintodo/api/tasks.py, registered in main.py (import + tags_metadata entry + include_router), reuses the existing get_store/get_current_user dependencies rather than inventing new wiring. Filters via GraphStore.list_nodes (unpaginated, in-memory filter) rather than a new Cypher query shape - acceptable at the "today" working-set scale, documented as a scope note in the function docstring for a future session to revisit if it becomes a bottleneck. 7 new tests in tests/test_tasks_api.py: excludes idea-nodes, includes overdue+due-today, excludes future-dated and no-due-date tasks, excludes completed tasks (exercises F025), owner scoping, and 401 without auth. Test dates computed relative to datetime.now(UTC).date() rather than hardcoded, so the suite does not silently start failing on a future run date. Fast suite: 117 -> 124 passed. Full suite: 141 -> 148 passed, 1 skipped. ruff check . -> clean (caught and fixed DTZ011 naive date.today() usage in both the implementation and the tests mid-session, replaced with datetime.now(UTC).date()). mypy src tests -> 0 errors, 87 files.
